title: Kernel handoff & shedding sandbox
content:
Context and goal:
This is a working sandbox doc for reproducing and instrumenting a class of service-impacting slowdowns we suspect are caused by: (a) kernel handoff hysteresis between FlashAttention and paged/fallback kernels, and (b) shedding/queue behavior when small-batch storms hit fused-op paths. Aim is to capture reproducible traces, propose lightweight mitigations, and ship a minimal experiment in staging to validate.

High-level hypothesis (summary):
- When request mix rapidly shifts between long-context streaming (favoring FlashAttention) and short-response bursts (favoring fused small-batch kernels), the runtime's kernel-selection hysteresis plus KV-cache priming causes temporary throughput collapse and 95/99th latency spikes.
- Additionally, when fused-op codepaths are used concurrently with FlashAttention, small-batch scheduling leads to head-of-line blocking (microstutter) because the scheduler defers prefetch/batching decisions until kernel handshake completes.

Observed symptoms (from INF-1426 incident):
- 3x jump in token tail latencies for ~2–6s windows, correlated with fleet-wide model-switch events (canary rollouts).
- GPU utilization decreases ~20–35% during spikes while queue length and per-request CPU time increase.
- Trace shows many short-lived CUDA streams and repeated kernel-launch fallback sequences.

Repro plan (local staging harness):
1) Workload mix generator: two concurrent clients
   - LongCtxClient: streaming requests with 4096 token history, generate 1–2 responses / sec (simulate chat long context).
   - ShortBurstClient: fire 8–12 short completion requests (<=32 tokens) in tight loops with bursts every 1s.
2) Model binary: v2-small-fuse (has both FlashAttention and fused-op implementations); fallback enabled.
3) Runtime flags (tweakable):
   - KERNEL_HYSTERESIS_MS (default 1000) -> start testing 0/100/2000ms
   - PREFETCH_THRESHOLD_TOKENS -> 128/512/2048
   - FUSE_SCHED_WINDOW_MS -> 5/20/100
   - KV_PRIME_ON_SWITCH=true/false
4) Capture: per-request trace (trace-id), GPU kernel timelines (nsight-like), CUDA stream counts, per-kernel durations, queue length and batch sizes.

Key instrumentation to add (low-effort):
- Add a short-lived epoch id to traces when kernel selection changes for a model-version; emit event: "kernel_selection:FLASH->PAGED" with reason code.
- Emit small-batch decisions: when a request is appended to a batch vs. when it is dispatched alone.
- Expose scheduler state in /debug/scheduler (JSON lines) for short windows (not enabled in prod by default).

Preliminary microbench experiments (results snapshot)
- Baseline: HYST=1000ms, PREFETCH=512, SCHED=20ms
  - Tail P95 token-latency: 120ms
  - GPU util: 78% steady, drops to 52% during handoff window
  - Observed repeated kernel switch events ~3–6 events per 4s window
- Aggressive-no-hysteresis: HYST=0ms
  - P95 improved to 85ms, but increased CPU spin and kernel churn (kernel-launch rocket)
  - GPU util: 76% but higher variance
- High-prefetch: PREFETCH=2048
  - Lower kernel switches (primed KV), but cold-start cost increased for short bursts: P50 improved, P95 slightly worse for ShortBurstClient
- Small SCHED window (SCHED=5ms)
  - Reduced head-of-line time but increased number of tiny kernels -> GPU inefficiency overall

Trace excerpt (condensed):
[2025-09-12T13:22:41Z] req=abc123 model=v2-small-fuse selection=FLASH launch=flash_attn_kern(12us) seq=10
[2025-09-12T13:22:41Z] req=abc124 model=v2-small-fuse selection=DECIDE fallback_reason=kv_miss launch=paged_attn_kern(78us) seq=2
[2025-09-12T13:22:42Z] POLICY: hysteresis expired for model v2-small-fuse, switching to FLASH (epoch->E3)
[2025-09-12T13:22:42Z] scheduler: batch_id=567 appended req=abc128 size=1 (emit_delay=18ms)

Root-cause hypotheses (detailed):
1) Selection hysteresis interval too long: prevents switching to the more efficient kernel for the current mix quickly enough, causing temporary misalignment between batch sizes and kernel assumptions.
2) KV prime-on-switch race: when switching back to FlashAttention, KV priming is synchronous and blocks mainstream scheduling, causing backlog and then many tiny kernels post-prime.
3) Fuse path handshake: fused-op kernels perform an eager resource reservation on a small subset of CUDA streams, blocking other kernels until handshake completes. In presence of short bursts, that handshake has higher contention cost than its throughput benefit.
4) Scheduler default window tuned for throughput (favoring coalescing) but not for mixed workloads; leads to head-of-line blocking for short urgent requests.

Mitigations to evaluate (ranked):
- Fast path: reduce KERNEL_HYSTERESIS_MS to 100ms for models tagged as mixed-workload-capable. (Low risk)
- Async KV priming: change prime to background prefetch w/ low-priority queue so it doesn't block scheduler; allow first few requests to fall back but keep service responsive. (Medium effort)
- Preemptible handshake: allow fused-op handshake to be interruptible by a high-priority short-burst queue; postpone full reservation for non-urgent work. (Higher effort)
- Adaptive sched window: runtime auto-tunes FUSE_SCHED_WINDOW_MS based on observed short-burst ratio (start with short window when short-burst ratio > 20%). (Medium effort)
- Instrumentation-driven release: add fingerprinting that detects repeated kernel switches and temporarily forces the stable pipeline until utilization stabilizes. (Low effort, operational knob)

Safety and perf regressions to watch for:
- Too aggressive hysteresis removal increases kernel churn and driver-level overheads -> higher CPU and possibly context-switch overheads.
- Async priming might increase token cost if priming loads unused cache lines for models with very different attended keys.
- Preemptible handshake complexity could introduce new deadlocks; must have strong invariants and watchdog.

Short action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Ava] Build workload generator and synthetic harness (target: 2025-09-05)
- [Diego] Add trace events for kernel selection changes (PR draft: linked_artifacts PR/2178) (target: 2025-09-07)
- [Priya] Prototype async KV priming patch in fork and run microbench on 1xA100 staging node (target: 2025-09-10)
- [Evan] Implement adaptive sched window collector + simple heuristic (target: 2025-09-12)
- Run 5x experiments across different flag combinations and capture traces for root-cause analysis meeting (target: 2025-09-15)

Experiment notes and reproducibility tips:
- Use --trace-sample 1.0 for these experiments (capture all) and rotate traces every 10MB to avoid disk blowup.
- When trying HYST=0, cap concurrent clients to 200 to avoid OOM on CPU side (kernel churn spikes!).
- Use nsys-style timeline view and filter kernels by name prefix 'flash'/'paged'/'fused' to see handoff windows.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Is KV priming in the runtime already async in other codepaths (see similar logic in quantized kernels)? If so, replicate pattern.
- How does model-seeded cache eviction interact with priming? Could priming thrash other models' KV caches under multi-tenant nodes?
- Does GPU driver version change the observed behavior (test on 525 vs 535)?

Meeting notes template for RCA (to fill post experiments):
- Incident summary (timeline)
- Repro steps and flags used
- Key traces and visualizations (attach links)
- Candidate mitigations + perf tradeoffs
- Decision and rollout plan (canary strategy, telemetry to watch)

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Run harness: ./tools/handshake_harness --model v2-small-fuse --long-clients 50 --short-clients 300 --duration 120s --flags "KERNEL_HYSTERESIS_MS=1000;PREFETCH_THRESHOLD_TOKENS=512"
- Collect traces: ./bin/trace_collector --out traces/handshake-run1 --filter "model=v2-small-fuse" --nsys
- Simple analysis: jq -r '.events[] | select(.type=="kernel_switch") | [.ts,.req,.from,.to] | @tsv' traces/handshake-run1.jsonl | column -t

Notes to future reader: this doc is intentionally a sandbox — prefer small, reversible runtime changes in staging. We should prioritize mitigations that keep correctness and have a clear rollback path.
